cells.tense: You're holding what you're responsible for, and the holding is steady.
cells.ask: show one person what the tending has cost, and let them honor it
cells.core:
You're tending what's yours to tend — the people, the work, the things that grow because you keep showing up for them. The care doesn't exhaust you and the weight doesn't bend you. You decide what needs doing and you do it, and the load stays yours to carry.

The next thing this steadiness is free to feed is being seen for it. Let someone know what the holding has taken from you. Not to be repaid — so the cost of the care becomes visible and honored, and the release that comes at the end of a thing well tended can run its course.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what you tend, and you carry it well.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that holds up under weight

cells.tense: You're already carrying loads that haven't arrived yet.
cells.ask: put the weight down and let yourself imagine how this ends well
cells.core:
You're standing ahead of yourself, holding up what hasn't happened yet — the need before it's spoken, the failure before it starts, the collapse before there's any sign of one. You're tending futures that haven't been planted, and the endurance is going out ahead of you. The care that should be steady has become a grip.

What you're actually reaching for is the deep satisfaction of seeing something you imagined come all the way through — the load finished, not just borne. Let yourself picture that, fully, before you take on more. Vision like that comes from having lived through enough, not from bracing. When you can dream it instead of guard against it, your hands come off the grip.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying weight nobody's handed you yet.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that holds up under weight

cells.tense: You set it down a while back, and you're still standing where you set it down.
cells.ask: pick one thing you tend and let it show you it's still alive
cells.core:
You can hold what must be held — that hasn't gone anywhere — but you stopped picking things up. Not because you can't, but because it's been a while since you let yourself tend anything you actually care about. The holding happens, the choosing doesn't.

What's missing is the reason to keep going: the strength that comes from still wanting the thing. So don't push yourself into the work. Go look at one thing you've kept alive — a person, a habit, a growing thing — and let it show you it's still there. The want comes back before the strength does.
cells.sheetLine: You can still hold it. You've stopped picking it up.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that holds up under weight

cells.tense: You're already holding it — you just haven't put your name on the holding.
cells.ask: say out loud which part of this you're choosing, and let it count
cells.core:
Holding what must be held is what you do, and you do it well — you stay with the work, the people, the things that would fall apart if you stepped away. You can carry a lot without breaking, and you keep choosing to carry it, day after day.

And still it gets described as just what has to be done. Responsibilities, not decisions. The care is real and constant, and the choosing inside it goes unnamed — even to you. Tell someone one thing you keep going that you could have let drop, and mean it as yours. When the cost is seen and honored, the release at the end of it stops feeling like defeat.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying this. You haven't said it's yours.

cells.place: in the part of you that holds up under weight
